title: SpaceX pursues US$40 billion Nvidia chip financing while Terafab charts path to AI compute independence
content: SpaceX is reportedly seeking US$40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips, a massive capital commitment driven by surging artificial intelligence (AI) computing demand. Viewed alongside Elon Musk's Terafab semiconductor manufacturing initiative, however, the move suggests a dual-track strategy: relying on Nvidia for near-term computing capacity while gradually reducing dependence on external suppliers over the longer term.

title: Ledlink hits record revenue as automotive optics and AI server components fuel growth
content: LED lens manufacturer Ledlink Optics reported record monthly and quarterly revenue in September and the third quarter of 2026, respectively, driven by sustained demand for automotive optical lenses and steadily increasing shipments of precision structural components for AI servers.

title: Bloom Energy SOFC system to support AOI's Taiwan expansion

title: US and 14 nations issue statement on overcapacity, target semiconductors
content: The US and 14 other economies issued a joint statement after the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee, pledging to work together on structural overcapacity and excess production in key industries. They singled out autos, EVs, batteries, chemicals, semiconductors and solar panels.

title: Infineon completes acquisition of C2i to expand AI data center power capabilities
content: Infineon has finished acquiring India-based C2i Semiconductors, a maker of software-defined multiphase controllers and smart power stages used in AI data centers. The acquisition indicates the growing importance of power stability and efficiency as the number of energy-hungry AI processors rises.

title: AI PCs face memory squeeze as server demand takes priority
content: Microsoft's October 7 opening of pre-orders for Surface Laptop Ultra, featuring up to 128GB of unified memory, highlights a potential new source of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) demand as PC makers bring larger AI models and autonomous agents onto local devices. But the opportunity comes as PC shipments decline and memory manufacturers prioritize server customers, raising questions about whether high-capacity PCs can secure enough supply to become a meaningful growth market.

title: TSMC's third-quarter revenue rises 51% to NT$1.49 trillion as September sales stay near record
content: TSMC reported consolidated revenue of about NT$511.86 billion (approx. US$16.1 billion) for September 2026. That was up 54.6% from NT$330.98 billion a year earlier and down 0.6% from August, the company said on October 8.

title: Hanmi wins rare Samsung order amid US$5 billion chip substrate expansion
content: South Korea's Hanmi Semiconductor has secured a KRW24.48 billion (approx. US$18.3 million) equipment order from Samsung Electro-Mechanics, a rare deal with a Samsung Group affiliate after years of limited business following a patent dispute. The contract comes a week after Samsung Electro-Mechanics announced a KRW6.78 trillion expansion of its AI server substrate business, as demand for advanced chip packaging continues to grow.

title: India's chip packaging plants start exporting, but scale, skills, and subsidies test the next phase
content: India's outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) sector has moved from inaugurations to its first export shipments. The challenge now is scale. The new plants are small, still lean on foreign engineers and partners, and the government's second subsidy round offers less support for conventional packaging than the first. Japanese chipmakers are among the earliest customers, but they are spreading work across several Indian partners rather than building their own plants.

title: China pushes six-network buildout as AI strains power links
content: China is accelerating construction of its so-called "six networks" — water, a new power grid, computing, next-generation communications, urban underground pipelines, and logistics — as data centers driven by AI and the digital economy create new demand for electricity and infrastructure. The latest push is turning coordination between computing, power, and telecommunications into a new policy challenge.

title: AUO subsidiary Darwin shifts toward high-end manufacturing, explores CPO and semiconductor opportunities
content: As AUO deepens its push into co-packaged optics (CPO), its subsidiary Darwin Precisions is also exploring opportunities in the semiconductor sector, leveraging its expertise in precision and ultra-precision machining and precision molds.

title: Sasken eyes reusable chip IP as India pushes beyond semiconductor design services
content: India-based engineering firm Sasken Technologies plans to license company-owned semiconductor interconnect intellectual property (IP) to multiple customers, marking an effort to move beyond customer-specific chip engineering work toward a reusable IP business model.

title: Samsung to exit in-house automotive AP, focus on high-margin chips
content: Samsung Electronics' System LSI division is reportedly planning a retreat from the automotive application processor (AP) business and launching a major restructuring, with a future focus on high-margin areas such as image sensors and mobile system-on-chip (SoC) products. Analysts say Samsung is seeking to improve profitability in its non-memory businesses through a selection and concentration strategy after years of losses at System LSI and its foundry operations.
